newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Slow passage of Venezuela labor law reform seen.
newsitem.headline: Slow passage of Venezuela labor law reform seen.

text.p: Reform of Venezuela's Labor Law, the first step in a ground-breaking overhaul of the country's social security system agreed by government, private sector and union officials in mid-March, will take at least one month, legislators said.
"Twenty two days have already passed since the agreement was announced," Ramon Guillermo Aveledo, president of the Chamber of Deputies, told Reuters. "We can't be expected to take less time."
The government presented the proposed Labor Law changes on Tuesday to a special Commission in Congress for wider discussion.
The Commission can decide to give the bill special urgency, in which case it will be okayed by the Chamber of Deputies within ten days before going to the Senate.
"The Senate will then decide for itself whether to give the bill the same treatment," said Avelado.

Normally, Venezuelan legislation returns to the Chamber of Deputies for a second discussion, and thence the Senate once again, before it is passed. But passage of any bill can be sped by a Bicameral debate on the second time round.
"We all want to bill's approval to come soon, but it's not possible to estimate dates," he added.
